text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- NATO admits three Eastern European states.
- Palestinian Authority police intervene in Russian Church property dispute in Hebron.
- Israel: Lebanon violated Grapes of Wrath deal.
- Knesset creates Rabin memorial day.
- Treasury considers slashing tax benefits.
- Tower semiconductor to discuss grants, tax waivers for $1 billion investment.
HAARETZ
- Round of government appointments to be brought for Knesset approval this morning.
- Top PLO official in Jerusalem Faisal al-Husseini plans to build a belt of Palestinian neighbourhoods around Jerusalem.
- Defence Minister Mordechai and PLO negotiator Shaath to meet this evening in bid to advance phased strategies to renew peace talks.
- Coalition deal with Gesher will cost up to 2 billion shekels. Treasury: they didn't consult with us.
- Argument continues on independence of Bank of Israel.
- Communications Minister Limor Livnat: Bezek International offers minimum prices only for its subscribers and misled the public.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Price of Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition promises: 3 billion shekels.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu promises 'new page' in way government works.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel officials: Bank of Israel will not intervene in forex trading even during sharp swings.
- Merger between Israel Aircraft Industries factory and Elbit company.
